steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Ugh, my tail's all wet.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Nothing's changed at all. Neither these filthy streets, nor this damned rain.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Dunno what it is, but even though the snow in Ursus can kill people, the rain here's somehow more unpleasant.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Hope there's a hairdryer at my master's place...
Her master's house is located at the end of this alley. Years ago, Crownslayer stormed off in a rage to prove that she was strong enough to take revenge on the conspiracies looming over her.
Now, Lyudmila has returned once more. Whether or not her efforts have poked a hole through that gloomy sky, she cannot yet say.
Possibly, nothing at all has changed. Possibly, she has become an accomplice to an even greater calamity.
But luckily, Lyudmila is still able to return to this place. She thinks to herself, surely her teacher will be able to tell her what to do next.
At that moment, she suddenly feels a chill.
At first, Lyudmila assumes it is because she is nervous about facing her teacher again.
But just as quickly, she realizes that she was wrong.
She starts to shake uncontrollably, on the spot.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Maestro!
The thick, inescapable stench of blood.
Her teacher lies face-up on the ground, fresh blood still flowing outward and spreading.
A small knife has been dropped nearby.
Lyudmila tries to approach and stifle her teacher's still-bleeding wound, but she finds herself unable to move a single step, unable to even tear away her gaze.
From the shadows wafts an aura that is both familiar and terrifying to her.
A wolf with gray hair, wearing a red hoodie.
The true wolf is dead. I did as Grandmother asked.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: It's you.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: What... have you done?!

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: I am a wolf hunter. I do as Grandmother asks.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: The true wolf is dead. The true wolf did not fight.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Cazzo!

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: I'll kill you!

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: Hm... I promised Kal'tsit to only kill wolves. You are not a wolf.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: Hm. Was she your Kal'tsit? That's why you smell of wolf.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: *gasp*... *gasp*... You know she couldn't fight anymore, so why?!

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: Grandmother said. These are the rules of the game.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: And now, she's out.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: I have to go. There are other wolves here. I have to find them.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: (Sniffs the air.)

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: But, another wolf is out of the game. Is someone faster than me?

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: Don't you dare leave!
The wolf in the red hoodie does not respond to Lyudmila's cries. She hums a fragmented ditty, flitting past Lyudmila with brisk steps.
Lyudmila's outstretched hand grasps only thin air.
She suddenly remembers what her teacher once told her:

a.text: 'Lyudmila, do you know what it means to be my student?'
'I'm become decrepit and weak now. Are you still willing to be my student, and my tool?'

steps.text: Lyudmila falls to her knees.

steps.name: Lyudmila
steps.text: 'Drink deep of the suffering of the deceased'...

steps.name: Excited Audience Member
steps.text: A performance worthy of Signorina Caterina! Well worth the wait!

steps.name: Excited Audience Member
steps.text: So we finally know that Cellinia, the ideal Siracusan, was just a fantasy concocted by the collective Siracusan consciousness.

steps.name: Excited Audience Member
steps.text: But because she was so well-known by the public as a symbol of perfection, her existence was reasonable enough to explain away through the common imagination.

steps.name: Excited Audience Member
steps.text: I was blown away by the big reveal at the end. She never existed at all!

steps.name: Excited Audience Member
steps.text: What a profound conclusion.

steps.name: Excited Audience Member
steps.text: After the incident with that broadcast a while ago, and everything that followed over the next twelve hours, I thought that was going to be the end of Volsinii.

steps.name: Excited Audience Member
steps.text: But despite all that, here we are enjoying such a fantastic production. Così è la vita!

steps.name: Enthusiastic Audience Member
steps.text: You can say that again.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Audience Member
steps.text: Phew, I thought the sky was going to fall.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Audience Member
steps.text: Who would've ever expected things to unfold like that?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Audience Member
steps.text: So, are you planning to move over to the new city?

steps.name: Excited Audience Member
steps.text: Depends. But, if Signorina Caterina's plays are still available over in the new city, I could see myself heading over.

steps.name: Excited Audience Member
steps.text: A city without famiglie, huh? Growing up, I never even dared to imagine a future like that.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Audience Member
steps.text: Now that you mention it...

steps.name: Enthusiastic Audience Member
steps.text: Did you know that Signorina Caterina is working on something completely new?

steps.name: Excited Audience Member
steps.text: A new production?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Audience Member
steps.text: That's right. The title of it alone is enough to get my blood pumping.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Audience Member
steps.text: It's called: 'I Siracusani.'
A shovel digs into the dirt. Then again.
Leontuzzo is struggling to dig a grave in the cemetery.
Next to him is a coffin in which his father, Bernardo, sleeps.
Today is the funeral of Bernardo, the former don of Famiglia Bellone.
A funeral for one of the Dodici dons should have seen the entire cemetery packed to the fences.
But, not a single soul will mourn the passing of a man who betrayed his famiglia, his city, and his society.
Leontuzzo also asked Lavinia and the others not to come.
This is his last farewell to his father.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Padre mio, how would you be seen by future generations?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: As a man who ushered in a new era, or as a man who betrayed the old one?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I guess that all depends on how well I do, haha.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You've passed one hell of a weight onto my shoulders.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But, I guess that means I'm a worthy son. And that I'm a sucker here to clean up your mess.
Leontuzzo continues to chat animatedly as if his father is still alive with him as he digs.
But other than that, he doesn't know what else to say.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Oh right, Signora Sicilia agreed to my request.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: There will be no famiglie in the new nomadic city.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I guess a part of your dream did come true.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: After talking with Signora Sicilia, I think I finally understand her a bit better.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Seems like she wouldn't mind taking Siracusa with her to the grave.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: It doesn't bother her at all that Siracusa can only enjoy a semblance of peace while she's alive, because for her, Siracusa doesn't need a future.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: How should I put this...? Signora Sicilia is more like the caretaker of a bygone era than an actual ruler.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The reason she was willing to give me a chance was just because she decided it was worth a try. Nothing more, nothing less.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: What a terrifying being.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Phew... I thought I'd be here all day digging your grave, but it turns out it wasn't so hard.
Enough space has been made in the ground to accommodate the coffin. The last thing that remains is to lower it in.
Leontuzzo walks to the front of the coffin, hesitates for a moment, but finally reaches out his hands.
The coffin is extremely heavy, and pushing it is a very demanding task.
Just as his strength is about to waver, he is suddenly joined by a pair of helping hands.
Leontuzzo turns his head, and sees Demetri right next to him.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Demetri, you...
Demetri says nothing, simply taking an object that shines with a silvery light out from his coat and tossing it into the grave.
It's a pocket watch.

a.text: The Don... he gave it to me.
And now, I guess it's been returned to its original owner.
You've already apologized to me, Leontuzzo.
But, even if I can forgive you, our fratelli who died in that conflict could never forgive you.
Even if Famiglia Bellone is gone, I won't forget them.
I hear you plan to organize a new famiglia.
Most of the guys who survived left already, but some stayed behind, and they need a place to go.
Even for you, that's one ass-backwards famiglia.
You're walking down a thorny path.
And eventually, I will stand in your way.
So, don't go dying on me.

steps.text: The rain continues to come down hard, but Leontuzzo can still faintly hear a soft 'Leon' at the end of that last sentence.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Same to you, Demetri.
He lifts his head, and lets the raindrops strike his face.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You won't be needing most of this furniture anymore, right?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Guess not. Famiglia Bellone is no more.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Most of the old associates have already left. After all... it's not an easy thing to stomach getting betrayed by your own don.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Bernardo, who practically stood on the highest pinnacle of a famiglia's rule, has repudiated the very existence of famiglie.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: He also repudiated many things once seen as priceless.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Honor, trust, loyalty, dedication to the famiglia...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Did my father teach each and every wise guy those rules without ever believing in them himself?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...I don't know.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I've been thinking a lot about it, the last few days. Did I ever know the real Bernardo Bellone?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The artistic director of Compagnia dell'alba was one mask that he wore. The cunning Don Bellone was another.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Then, is it not possible that the smiling, bright-eyed Bernardo who once shared his ideals with me was just another mask?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But, it doesn't matter. Not anymore.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Leon, the two of you, together, gave a chance for that new city to truly be born.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I guess so.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The movers will be here soon.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: None of this has been in vain, Leon.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: In the new city area... Or, I guess it's a proper city now, we'll build something new.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Something brand new, that Siracusa has never seen before.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: An order that belongs to everyone.
Leontuzzo looks at Lavinia, his eyes shining with determination.
Each wolf, from its moment of birth, knows that its existence is a symbol of the wastelands.
After countless eras and countless conflicts, they finally selected the alpha wolf through the rules of the game as it had been played up to that point.
For Zaaro, his defeat this round was, undoubtedly, a disgrace.
But they will continue to live on.
As long as there is another round of the game to be played, he will stage his comeback in time.
To this end, he has already started searching for suitable candidates.
And almost immediately, he found Lappland, wandering the wastes after having left Volsinii.
However—

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Are you done napping yet, Zaaro?
Zaaro and Lappland have been fighting in the wastes for the past three months.
During that time, Zaaro had countless opportunities to sink his fangs into the neck of this madwoman.
There was no way for her to defeat him.
But, he gradually comes to realize, it is actually he who has no way of defeating her.
No thought can be nourished in her blood and sinew, no victory can be proclaimed in her head, and no meaning can be derived from her death.
She is an empty husk that has been filled.
Is she also the wastes?
No, she is an overgrowth.
He understands in an instant that if Bernardo's betrayal was an unexpected act of rationality, the being before him is completely beyond his comprehension.
No, he has seen humans like her before. She is hardly unique.
But at this unique point in time, she indeed is the only such one before him.
An omen.
A summon.
And thus, for the first time in thousands of years and perhaps the last time, the incarnation of the wastes lies down next to a human being.
He chooses to surrender his dignity to the unknown.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Done fighting?

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Our battle will continue for thousands upon thousands of years.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Until the victor is decided, I will walk with you.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Hah. Whatever you say.
Lappland's weapons slip from her grasp. She has already lost consciousness.
Before she falls, Zaaro walks over and supports her body with his own, as if it is the most natural thing to do.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Texas, we've chosen different paths to destroy Siracusa.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I'm so looking forward to seeing you again.
She closes her eyes, and falls into a deep slumber.
The vast wilderness is completely devoid of anything else. For a brief moment, it seems as if all existence between heaven and earth is but one human and one wolf.
